sample_unit: model evaluations (14 LLMs x 100 questions x 5 runs)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across 5 repeated runs (Fleiss' kappa, coefficient of variation)
links.effect: Proprietary models kappa 0.84 vs open-source 0.70; stability varied from CV 0.00% (Falcon H1) to CV 32.2% (Mistral Medium).
links.quote: Stability varied, ranging from consistent error in Falcon H1 (CV = 0.00%) to erratic instability in Mistral Medium (Mistral AI, Paris, France) (CV = 32.2%).

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on PSITE exam questions, as a proxy for clinical competence
links.effect: Claude Opus 4.5 90.2% and GPT-5.2 Pro 87.0%; proprietary mean 76.1% vs open-source 60.2%. Authors state accuracy alone is insufficient to judge clinical utility.
links.quote: Accuracy alone is insufficient to judge clinical utility; stability metrics are essential for selecting AI tools in surgical education.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance, reliability, and stochastic variability of 14 large language models on plastic surgery training examination questions (PSITE) without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
